data.narrative:
Constellr, a Series A space and aerospace company founded by Max Gulde and Marius Bierdel, has raised €37M to date. The valuation landscape includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) trading at a median P/S multiple of 27.4x, and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs. However, the narrow peer set at identical stage limits direct multiples-based anchoring.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proves applicable. Using total capital raised (€37M) as a value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields €74M. Peer-median methodology was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data in the Space & Aerospace sector. Public-comp anchoring could not be deployed absent the target's revenue, a standard constraint in private company valuation.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of €63M (low) to €85M (high), with a median of €74M. This range carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method and the absence of revenue visibility. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector and stage, market conditions affecting Space & Aerospace multiples, and undisclosed traction metrics that would enable peer or public-comp approaches.
